name: Learn cross-stitch
blurb: The most forgiving needlecraft: a counted grid, one stitch, and a chart that tells you exactly what to do. Genuinely relaxing and almost impossible to do badly once you can count.
gear: Stranded floss and a blunt tapestry needle
A hoop and a printed chart
steps: Learn to find the centre of both the fabric and the chart, and always start there.
Learn the stitch: a row of half-crosses in one direction, then back over them to complete each X.
Keep every top stitch going the same direction across the whole piece — this is what makes it look even.
Learn to carry thread short distances on the back and when to finish off instead.
Add back-stitch outlining last, which is what makes the design read clearly.
Wash, press face-down on a towel, and frame it.
tips: Count twice before stitching a new area. Unpicking counted work is miserable.
Never carry dark thread across pale unstitched fabric; it shows through.
proof: A finished small design with consistent stitch direction and correct counting throughout.
